universal_frames.name: Lava World / Pre-Terraforming Survey
required_truths: Universal is still a lava-based planet.
Off-world expeditions may reach, study, exploit, seed, or establish habitats on it.
Later habitable Universal has not yet formed.

universal_frames.name: Terraforming and First Habitats
required_truths: Planetary change and engineered ecology are active processes.
Early habitat, biosphere, and settlement decisions can shape later history.

universal_frames.name: Medieval Universal Before Architect Imprisonment
required_truths: The frame may begin about 200 years before the Architects are imprisoned.
The Architects are not yet in the later prison state.
Medieval societies exist under period-appropriate Architect pressure.

universal_frames.name: Imprisonment and Architectfall
required_truths: Architect prisons, Ichor, rebellion, and Architect-subject power relationships are central.
Modules must declare which Architect masks are free, imprisoned, defeated, absent, or transformed.

universal_frames.name: Ichor-Industrial and Transitional Universal
required_truths: Thundercoils, engineered systems, factions, and Architect contamination affect daily life.

universal_frames.name: Post-Architect Mask Defeat
required_truths: The Architect masks have been defeated according to the campaign’s established outcome.
Communities and institutions must replace, inherit, reject, or dismantle Architect systems.

universal_frames.name: Universalian Spacefaring
required_truths: Universalians reach their own interplanetary and interstellar stage after the Architect masks are defeated.
Spacefaring is not retroactively credited to the Architect masks.

universal_frames.name: Galactic Settlement Network
required_truths: Universalians and off-world civilizations share, contest, or connect settlements and political futures.
A module declares which expeditions arrived before terraforming and which relationships formed later.

cross_era_rule.core: Field rank remains valid; unfamiliar context may impose one Burden.

campaign_spans.name: Pre-Terraform Period
campaign_spans.scope: Lava-world surveys, extraction, first contact, Thay’lmériûn sect rivalries, the theft of experimental genomes, and stolen terraforming systems before a habitable biosphere.

campaign_spans.name: Terraforming and First Habitats
campaign_spans.scope: Planetary engineering, habitat survival, ecological choices, and the construction of feeding ecosystems and permanent habitats.

campaign_spans.name: Age of the Twenty-Two Masks
campaign_spans.scope: The twenty-two dissident Thay’lmériûn sect members present themselves as gods, bind class channels to their cult identities, and build feeding institutions.

campaign_spans.name: Medieval Universal
campaign_spans.scope: Fortifications, guilds, provinces, ritual technology, Thundercoils, hidden alien infrastructure, and resistance.

campaign_spans.name: Industrial to Orbital Transition
campaign_spans.scope: Mass production, electrification, launch capacity, public discovery of old systems, and contested planetary governance.

campaign_spans.name: Interstellar and Galactic Settlement
campaign_spans.scope: Starships, colonies, diplomacy, lost settlements, Architect remnants, and the ethics of creating new biospheres.

colony_rule: Each track is a 4-, 6-, 8-, or 12-segment clock. A colony can advance unevenly; high technology does not automatically produce just governance or ecological care.

metadata.title: Universal Time and Era Conversion
metadata.purpose: Conversions among rounds, Beats, rests, journeys, downtime, projects, campaign years, and WorldBuilder eras.

play_time_scales.procedure: Route choices, roles, Supply, hazard clocks
Projects, recovery, faction and settlement turns

combat_time.reaction_window: From the end of a creature's turn until the start of its next turn.

breather.benefit: spend one Hit Die or clear 1 Stress

benefits: heal to half HP then spend Hit Dice

journey_time.unit: watch or travel day, chosen to match the fiction
journey_time.supply: 1 Supply supports 1 character for 1 travel day or one party requirement.

paces.cautious: Edge on hazard tests; uses 2 Supply
paces.urgent: Fill 1 Progress and 1 Danger; prevents a full Field Rest

campaign_years.advancement_note: Era change is a Legacy-scale project rather than an instant global rewrite.

time.era_meaning: Common access, infrastructure, training, replacement parts, and social assumptions—not personal worth or automatic combat superiority.
time.local_variation: Settlements may combine technologies from different eras; the global Era is a common ceiling, not compulsory uniformity.

blocks.text: Build weapons from function rather than historical name.

rows.Properties: Near, two-handed, reload; one Burden at Far

blocks.text: A sword, vibroblade, fossil-tooth macuahuitl, and bounded plasma cutter can use the same profile with different tags. Superior technology changes access, range, armor interaction, sensors, maintenance, and Scale before it changes bounded personal damage.
Common tags include Aim, Arc, Automatic, Blast, Breach, Concealable, Defensive, Finesse, Forceful, Heavy, Integrated, Nonlethal, Reach, Reload, Silent, Thrown, Two-Handed, Unstable, and Versatile.

items: Aim: spend 1 Beat without moving to gain one Edge on the next attack this turn.
Automatic: spend 1 Supply or charge to Suppress a Near zone.
Blast: affects a Near point and adjacent Engaged targets; targets save for half if the effect permits.
Breach: counts as one Scale higher against objects, cover, and vehicles, not creatures.
Defensive: while wielded, Guard action also grants +1 Guard until next turn.
Forceful: on a Forceful Hit, push 10 feet instead of 5.
Reload: after a number of attacks set by the item, spend 1 Beat and ammunition/charge.
Unstable: a Crisis adds one Wear or Instability.

rows.Common limits: Strength or power requirement; Stealth Burden
Requires charge, maintenance, and Era access

blocks.text: Specific class dossiers or items may use familiar fifth-edition armor values. Choose one calculation; do not stack base AC formulas.
Use familiar coinage for ordinary purchases where it helps, but rare gear requires Availability as well as price.

rows.Meaning: License, guild, faction, or professional access
Mission, black market, state, temple, or military authority
Project, discovery, patron, or story reward

blocks.text: Supply abstracts ammunition, charge packs, consumable components, ordinary spare parts, and expedition necessities. A character carries PB Supply without using slots; extra Supply uses one carry slot each.

ownership.WorldBuilder: maps, terrain, weather, routes, geometry, pins and spatial state
ownership.LifeSimulation: peoples, NPCs, locations, goods, services, schedules, relationships, factions and living-world behavior
ownership.Architect Engine: tests, classes, resources, clocks, conflict, harm, advancement, alignment and campaign consequence

galaxy_names.referent: The name refers to the twenty-two beings remembered as gods and the predatory system they built around Universal.
galaxy_names.spacefaring_name_origin: Unknown. Interstellar usage predates surviving records; the original language and meaning are lost.
galaxy_names.universalian_name_origin: A Kaluseban expression that translates approximately as The Venus Fly Trap, referring to the Twenty-Two and the predatory trap built around Universal.

architect_origin.planet_after: lush greenhouse planet designed around dense ecosystems and long-term feeding
architect_origin.origin: Twenty-two dissident members of the larger Thay’lmériûn civilization.

worldbuilder_rules: A settlement, culture, faction, or NPC may reference a race_id without duplicating the race profile.
Biome preferences are generation weights, not prohibitions.
Architect terraforming responsibility, deity patronage, and race habitat remain separate IDs and fields.
Alien-Folk use Zešijómë as the broad interstellar galaxy name unless a local culture records another term.
